text:
Yan Kuznetsov has the tools you notice first. The 24-year-old Calgary defenseman, a 6-foot-4 second-round pick from 2020, skates faster at top speed than 93% of NHL players and has a shot harder than 92% of them (95.6 mph at his best). What the Flames are working out this season is how much of a regular he is. He has played every one of their last ten games at about 17 minutes a night, with four assists in 19 games, right on the median pace for defensemen drafted around his slot.

The results with him on the ice have been a little unlucky. Calgary takes 53% of the shot attempts at five on five when he plays, though only 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and the Flames have scored 4.0 fewer goals than those chances deserve while he is out there. Last season tells you both sides: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on than against most defensemen, while Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck into the zone on 42% of his entries rather than dumping it. The puck-carrying makes him interesting; the defending decides his minutes.
headline: Yan Kuznetsov's tools are clear, his role less so
